body.p: Rate of the biliary excretion, a half-life of pravastatin in the liver of about 7 min. It changes only the timing of the enterohepatic circulation, not the exposure, and is not fitted.
parameter controls genetic variants (1.0 reference function, < 1.0 reduced function, > 1.0 increased function)
Set to 3mM for reference state of 3mM in healthy patient as 3mM plasma LDL-C.
Feedback of complex to uptake. Mechanism?
Feedback of LDLR membrane on LDLR pool via equilibration constant. Keq = ldlr_membrane/ldlr_substrate
higher then HMG-CoA Reductase: 3E-3 [mmole/min/l] /1.4 [l]/ 0.03 [mole/l] = 71.4E-3 [1/min]
product inhibition ~ reference concentration
Import of pravastatin via OATP1B1 (SLCO1B1) from the plasma in the liver. Here the genetic variants of SLCO1B1 and the inhibition of OATP1B1 have their effects.

Irreversible import of pravastatin via Michaelis-Menten kinetics. The Km of 10 µM is far above the plasma concentrations (0.01-0.5 µM), so the uptake is linear and Vmax/Km sets the intrinsic clearance; the hepatic extraction is about 0.5 (F 0.17-0.18 with a fraction absorbed of 0.34, Singhvi1990).
Export of pravastatin via MRP2 from the liver into the bile, which flows into the intestinal lumen (enterohepatic circulation). Here the genetic variants of MRP2 have their effects.
Irreversible first order export.
